findings.statement: CXCR2 is the top convergence gene and is up in UC in all eight cohorts. In the same patients inflamed mucosa exceeds non-inflamed mucosa (paired log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972]), with only a small rise in non-inflamed versus control [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399]. The change holds after adjustment for segment, age and sex. Caveat for immune genes: a bulk increase can come from infiltrating neutrophils rather than a change inside the tissue, which the cell-context specialist should confirm.

CXCL8 (IL-8) is strongly and reproducibly raised in all eight cohorts, with a pooled log2FC given here [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.687]. As an immune-cell-rich chemokine, part of the bulk signal may come from infiltrating cells.

CD274 (PD-L1) is up in all eight cohorts and local to inflamed mucosa: paired inflamed versus non-inflamed log2FC [gene=CD274; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.0008], whereas non-inflamed versus control is barely changed [gene=CD274; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.1971]. This looks like an inflammation-driven response; immune-cell contribution to the bulk signal is possible.

IDO1 is up in all eight cohorts and the change replicates as protein in an independent proteomics study [gene=IDO1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.917].

CHI3L1 has one of the largest pooled increases [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.913], significant in all eight cohorts and robust to segment, age and sex adjustment. At protein level the direction agrees but the effect is much smaller [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607] and the authors did not call it significant, so the RNA magnitude overstates the protein change.

HMGCS2 is lost in all eight cohorts and the loss is specific to inflamed mucosa: non-inflamed versus control is flat [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649], while the paired inflamed versus non-inflamed contrast is strongly negative. Protein falls too [gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094] and the change holds after adjustment, making it a local-inflammation biomarker rather than a target.

AQP8 shows the largest pooled loss [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.7633], significantly down in all eight cohorts, making it a biomarker candidate rather than a target.

MMP3 is strongly induced [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.822] in all eight cohorts and is also higher in inflamed than non-inflamed mucosa of the same patient, in line with a tissue-remodelling programme.
DUOX2 rises in all eight cohorts [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.3033] and is higher in inflamed mucosa within patients, a local inflammation biomarker.

JAK2 has strong genetic and drug support but only a modest expression change [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.833], though significantly up in all eight cohorts. Its rank comes from genetics and tractability rather than expression magnitude.
S100A8 is up in all eight cohorts. As an immune-cell-rich gene, its bulk increase may partly reflect infiltrating cells, which the cell-context specialist should check.
TREM1 is up in all eight cohorts and higher in inflamed than non-inflamed mucosa; a phase 2 inhibitor (nangibotide) is listed. Its bulk rise may reflect infiltrating myeloid cells.

caveats: Pooled log2FC are on mixed RNA-seq and microarray scales; compare direction and significance across cohorts, not sizes. Heterogeneity (I2) is high for nearly all top genes.
Bulk RNA of inflamed mucosa includes infiltrating neutrophils and myeloid cells; CXCR2, CXCL8, S100A8, TREM1 and CD274 may reflect composition. The cell-context specialist must check.
Protein support is partial: only some genes are measured in the proteomics study, and the CHI3L1 protein effect was far smaller than the RNA effect.
Convergence ranking is driven by genetics and tractability for CXCR2, JAK2 and CD274.
Only CXCR2, CHI3L1 and HMGCS2 were tested with adjusted_change; only CHI3L1, IDO1 and HMGCS2 with protein_level.
